title: The deformation family is constant along the affine line
statement:
In the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], put $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$. Let $V,B$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $d\geq0$, and let $g:V\to B$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with a closed section $s:B\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], $g\circ s=\operatorname{id}_B$. Form the deformation family $F$ of [def-pur-dnc-section-family] and the section invariant $C(g,s)$ of [def-pur-section-invariant]. Let $a:\mathbf A^1_B\to B$ be the projection and $i_1:B\to\mathbf A^1_B$ its section $t=1$. Locally constant sheaves mean [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]; rank one means locally isomorphic to the constant module sheaf $\Lambda$. Twists are those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

1. *the family is a shift of a lisse line.* The family object
is a shift of a finite locally constant rank-one sheaf,
$$
F\simeq\mathcal L_F(d)[2d],
$$
and likewise $C(g,s)\simeq\mathcal L_1(d)[2d]$ on $B$; in
particular no descent of an object or of a morphism of a derived
category is needed below.
1. *constancy along the affine line.* There is a canonical
isomorphism
$$
\kappa:\;F\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;a^*C(g,s).
$$
Under the canonical identifications $i_1^*a^*C(g,s)\simeq C(g,s)\simeq i_1^*F$ of
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1), the family object is the
pullback of its own fibre at $t=1$: the deformation family is
constant along $\mathbf A^1_B$ over $B$.
1. *normalization and uniqueness.* $\kappa$ is the unique
isomorphism $F\to a^*C(g,s)$ which at the section $t=1$
restricts to the identity of $C(g,s)$ under the identification
$i_1^*F\simeq C(g,s)$ of
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1).
1. *locality and base change.* $\kappa$ is compatible with
etale localization on $B$ and with arbitrary base change
$B'\to B$.

proof.text: Use the finite coefficient ring $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ throughout. By [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](2), choose an etale covering $\{B_i\to B\}$ with relative coordinates of the pair near the section and with the induced DNC coordinates $u_j=x_j/t$. Refine the cover by affine etale neighborhoods $B_i$ of finite type over $B$, and write $U=\coprod_i B_i$. The cover members may be chosen affine open neighborhoods in the coordinate bases, hence separated finite type over $k$, as in the source proof Step 3. The map $U\to B$ is surjective etale; no finite-type hypothesis on $U$ is needed in the concentration lemma used in Step 3. The coordinates are etale maps of neighborhoods of the section, not assertions that the whole $V\times_B B_i$ is affine space. They give maps to the standard pair $(\mathbf A^d_{B_i},0)$ and, on its deformation, to the standard family $\mathbf A^d_{B_i}\times_{B_i}\mathbf A^1_{B_i}$; the section has $x_j=0$ and $u_j=0$. The DNC morphism is smooth of pure dimension $d$. By [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](2), its dualizing object, and that of $g$, are invertible. The current family-object formula of [def-pur-dnc-section-family] is $F=L\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g}$, on $\mathbf A^1_B$, and [def-pur-section-invariant] defines $C(g,s)=Ls^*\omega_g$ on $B$. The first formula is used only to identify the object whose local models are calculated in Step 2; the concentration and rank-one assertions are proved in Step 3, rather than taken from the definition. Base change of the etale cover to the affine line is again an etale cover by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]; both this cover and the original one are pro-etale covers by [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover].

source.place: Proof, main-20261015, Step 1: smoothness, coordinates and the already defined family object

proof.text: Write $F_i=F|_{\mathbf A^1_{B_i}}$ and $C_i=C(g,s)|_{B_i}$. Here is the dualizing comparison needed for the coordinate calculation. For an etale coordinate map $e:W\to X$, [lem-pur-co-smooth-etale-locality] gives cohomological smoothness and $\omega_e\simeq\Lambda_W$. For the smooth standard projection $p$, clauses (1), (2), and (3) of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] verify respectively the tensor-formula, invertibility, and base-change requirements of [def-pur-co-smoothness], so $p$ is cohomologically smooth. Those same three clauses applied to $g$ and to the smooth DNC projection show that they too are cohomologically smooth; thus the composition formula below also applies to the open coordinate inclusions into their sources. Apply [lem-pur-co-smooth-composition] to $e$ and $p$ to obtain $\omega_{pe}\simeq Le^*\omega_p$. The same formula for the open inclusion of a coordinate neighborhood into $V$ or into its deformation shows that pulling back to the section computes the original section invariant; the section factors through that neighborhood. Thus this calculation does not require an isomorphism of the entire pairs. The standard-pair calculation of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](4), or equivalently [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] for the standard projection, now gives isomorphisms $\alpha_i:F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_{B_i}}(d)[2d]$ and $\beta_i:C_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{B_i}(d)[2d]$. The base-change compatibility of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity], applied to the trivial rank-$d$ bundle along $a_i$ and then pulled back to its zero section, also identifies $a_i^*(\Lambda_{B_i}(d)[2d])\simeq\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_{B_i}}(d)[2d]$. This is the identification used in Step 4. The comparison of $F$ and $C$ with their restrictions after $B_i\to B$ is the arbitrary-base-change comparison of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](3). Ordinary constant-coefficient inverse image is exact and termwise on complexes by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

source.place: Proof, main-20261015, Steps 1 and 2: source-etale comparison and the standard-pair Thom calculation

proof.text: By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3), the finite-level twist $\Lambda(1)$ is a finite locally constant line; its tensor powers and duals, used in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], are again lines: on any cover trivializing the line these operations are just tensor powers and the dual of the free rank-one module. Consequently the local models of Step 2 are sheaves in degree $r=-2d$. Apply [lem-pur-concentrated-complex-shift](2) to $K=F$ and the surjective etale cover $\mathbf A^1_U\to\mathbf A^1_B$ with local sheaf $\Lambda(d)$, and to $K=C(g,s)$ and $U\to B$. It gives vanishing outside degree $-2d$ and finite local constancy of $M_F=\mathcal H^{-2d}(F)$ and $M_1=\mathcal H^{-2d}(C(g,s))$. These sheaves have rank one: their restrictions in Step 2 are $\Lambda(d)$, so further local trivializations are free of rank one. Part (1) of the same lemma gives $F\simeq M_F[2d]$ and $C(g,s)\simeq M_1[2d]$. Set $\mathcal L_F=M_F(-d)$ and $\mathcal L_1=M_1(-d)$. Cancellation of a line with its dual is the evaluation isomorphism, checked on a trivializing cover. Hence $F\simeq\mathcal L_F(d)[2d]$ and $C(g,s)\simeq\mathcal L_1(d)[2d]$, proving clause (1).

source.place: Proof, main-20261015, Step 1: reduction to actual sheaves by concentration in a single degree

proof.text: Let $\theta_i:i_1^*F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}C_i$ be the fibre identification of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1). From Step 2 set $\lambda_i=(a_i^*\beta_i)^{-1}\circ\alpha_i:F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}a_i^*C_i$, using the canonical identification $a_i^*(\Lambda_{B_i}(d)[2d])\simeq\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_{B_i}}(d)[2d]$ established in Step 2. Put $h_i=(i_1^*\lambda_i)\circ\theta_i^{-1}\in\operatorname{Aut}(C_i)$ and $\kappa_i=a_i^*(h_i^{-1})\circ\lambda_i$. Since $i_1^*a_i^*=\operatorname{id}$, we have $i_1^*\kappa_i=h_i^{-1}(h_i\theta_i)=\theta_i$. All maps used are isomorphisms. This normalization is composition with an automorphism and its inverse; no choice of a scalar on a connected component, and no additional trivialization of $C_i$, is required. The composition identifications used here are those of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], specialized to $a_i\circ i_1=\operatorname{id}_{B_i}$.

source.place: Proof, main-20261015, Step 2: explicit normalization of local comparisons at t=1

proof.text: These local comparisons also realize the punctured comparison used by the unit. Let $j:\mathbf G_{m,B}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_B$. By [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](3) there is a canonical $\kappa^\circ:j^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*a^*C(g,s)$; its restriction to $t=1$ is the same fibre identification $\theta$ of part (1), since both are the base-change identification on the fibre $(V,s)$. On $\mathbf G_{m,B_i}$ compare $j^*\kappa_i$ with $\kappa^\circ|_{\mathbf G_{m,B_i}}$. Step 3 writes their source and target as sheaves with the common shift $[2d]$. Removing that shift, the full faithfulness of the degree-zero embedding [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] (Stacks Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts (2)) identifies both maps with morphisms of finite locally constant sheaves. They agree at $t=1$ by Step 4. The second assertion of [lem-pur-lisse-uniqueness] therefore makes them equal on $\mathbf G_{m,B_i}$.

source.place: Unit sk-thm-dnc, Step 2; item Proof, main-20261015, Steps 2 and 3: punctured comparison and sheaf-level rigidity

proof.text: Apply [prop-pur-a1-invariance] with $Y=B$, $C=C(g,s)$, $\theta:i_1^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}C(g,s)$ from Step 4, and the cover $\{B_i\to B\}$ of Step 1. The required local shape is Step 3, with $m_i=d$ and $n_i=2d$. The normalized local comparisons are Step 4. All bases and cover members are separated finite type, and $F,C$ lie in the stated finite-Tor constructible categories by their defining setup. The gluing assertion gives $\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C(g,s)$ restricting to the $\kappa_i$, and its uniqueness assertion says it is the only isomorphism with $i_1^*\kappa=\theta$. Thus it is independent of the chosen cover, coordinates and initial local comparisons. This proves clauses (2) and (3). In terms of Step 3, this gluing is gluing maps of sheaves with a common shift; it does not assert descent for arbitrary objects or morphisms of derived categories. By Step 5 it extends $\kappa^\circ$.

source.place: Proof, main-20261015, Step 3: gluing and uniqueness; unit sk-thm-dnc, Step 3 before restricting to t=0

proof.text:
We record the comparison with the ordinary etale site needed only for unrestricted base change. For any scheme morphism $f:X	o S$, the definitions [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] give $f_{\mathrm{et},*}
u_{X,*}=
u_{S,*}f_{\mathrm{proet},*}$: at an etale object $U	o S$ both evaluate a pro-etale sheaf $H$ at $U	imes_S X$. By [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the adjunctions in those definitions, for any etale module sheaf $G$ and pro-etale module sheaf $H$ we consequently have natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*
u_S^*G,H)=\operatorname{Hom}(G,
u_{S,*}f_{\mathrm{proet},*}H)=\operatorname{Hom}(G,f_{\mathrm{et},*}
u_{X,*}H)=\operatorname{Hom}(
u_X^*f_{\mathrm{et}}^*G,H)$. Their identity elements give mutually inverse canonical comparisons $f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*
u_S^*\cong
u_X^*f_{\mathrm{et}}^*$. They respect the fixed scalar actions, since all the displayed functors act on those actions, and are natural in maps of sheaves. The composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition, lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] identify successive pullbacks. Their compatibility with this site comparison follows directly by adjunction: for two successive morphisms, either comparison is adjunct to the identity of the common composite right adjoint, so the two comparisons agree. For the identity morphism that adjunct is the identity, and the same Hom bijections send adjunction units to adjunction units. Taking a morphism and its section therefore respects the section identity on both sites. This is a formal adjunction calculation, with no geometric finiteness hypothesis.

source.place: Final base-change assertion: explicit comparison of ordinary and pro-etale inverse images by their adjunctions

proof.text: The arbitrary-base rigidity needed below is [lem-pur-a1-pullback-endomorphism-rigidity]: for every scheme $S$ and every finite locally constant pro-etale $\Lambda$-module sheaf $M$, an endomorphism of $p^*M$ on $\mathbf A^1_S$ which is the identity at $t=1$ is the identity. Here $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ is finite, so this applies to our coefficient ring. This generic sheaf statement has no finite-type restriction on $S$; it will be applied to $S=B'$ in Step 11.

source.place: Final base-change assertion: arbitrary-base endomorphism rigidity, extracted from former Step 8

proof.text: Let $b:B'\to B$ be arbitrary and let $b_1:\mathbf A^1_{B'}\to\mathbf A^1_B$ be its affine-line base change. By [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](5), the primed family and punctured comparison are the pullbacks of $F$ and $\kappa^\circ$. The fibre formula in part (1), together with [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], identifies the primed section invariant with $C'=b^*C(g,s)$ and its fibre comparison with $\theta'=b^*\theta$. Hence $\kappa'=b_1^*\kappa:F'\xrightarrow{\sim}a'{}^*C'$ is normalized by $\theta'$ and extends the primed punctured comparison. Exact termwise inverse image [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] pulls the Step 3 presentations back to $F'\simeq b_1^*M_F[2d]$ and $C'\simeq b^*M_1[2d]$. These are ambient derived inverse images when $B'$ is not finite type; no exceptional adjoint on a new constructible category is being assumed.

source.place: Final base-change assertion: pulled-back family, fibre and normalized map

proof.text: Put $M'=b^*M_1$. By [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin](b), choose a finite locally constant etale module sheaf $G$ on $B$ with $M_1\simeq\nu_B^*G$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-finite-locally-constant] with $T=Y=B$, $f=\operatorname{id}_B$, and $g=b$ to its underlying abelian sheaf. It says that $b_{\mathrm{et}}^*G$ is finite locally constant on $B'$. Its module structure is carried by inverse image, so it is a finite locally constant etale $\Lambda$-module sheaf. By Step 7, $M'\simeq\nu_{B'}^*b_{\mathrm{et}}^*G$; part (a) of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] now gives finite local constancy of $M'$ on the pro-etale site of $B'$. All three cited assertions apply to arbitrary schemes. This replaces the inline cover-and-finiteness argument of the former Step 9 by the existing pullback and comparison lemmas.

source.place: Final base-change assertion: finite lisse pullback, using existing lemmas

proof.text: For another normalized comparison $\eta:F'\xrightarrow{\sim}a'{}^*C'$, set $h=\eta\circ(\kappa')^{-1}$. Step 9 identifies its target with $a'{}^*M'[2d]$; cancel the shift and use [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to regard $h$ as an automorphism of the ordinary sheaf $a'{}^*M'$. Normalization says $i_1'{}^*h=\operatorname{id}_{M'}$. Step 10 verifies finite local constancy of $M'$, so [lem-pur-a1-pullback-endomorphism-rigidity] with $S=B'$, $p=a'$, $e=i'_1$ gives $h=\operatorname{id}$. Thus $\eta=\kappa'$. For successive base changes, the composite pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies the iterated pullback and the direct pullback as normalized comparisons; the same uniqueness makes them equal. Identity base change is the identity comparison. Etale localization is a special case. This proves clause (4), using no finite-type lisse-rigidity assertion over $B'$.

source.place: Final base-change assertion: uniqueness and compatibility for towers

    (θ : (L((AffineSpace.oneSection (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])).obj
      (D.familyObject Λ) ≅ sectionInvariant Λ g s) :
    ∃! κ : D.familyObject Λ ≅
        (L((𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin 1); B) ↘ B)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])).obj (sectionInvariant Λ g s),
      (L((AffineSpace.oneSection (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])).map κ.hom ≫

lean.note: Finite coefficient specialization Λ=A_{E,n}, with the concrete normalized Kummer Tate twist. The five declarations together give both lisse-line statements, constancy, normalization/uniqueness, and arbitrary base change. The finite-stage pro-etale category is read through its etale-origin presentation: see WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.Derived.Constructible and the fully faithful comparison in Derived.Comparison; comparison commutes canonically with pullback. The theorem is applied to the actual extended-Rees deformation datum constructed in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.DeformationSpace.Coordinates.nonempty_deformationToNormalConeData, and to the canonical fibre comparison, not to a freely chosen replacement of either object.

blueprint_update.statement:

[def-pur-dnc-section-family] with family object $F$, let
$a:\mathbf A^1_B\to B$ be the projection and let
$i_1:B\to\mathbf A^1_B$ be the section $t=1$.

1. *the family is a shift of a lisse line.* The family object
is a shift of a finite locally constant rank-one sheaf,
$$
F\simeq\mathcal L_F(d)[2d],
$$
and likewise $C(g,s)\simeq\mathcal L_1(d)[2d]$ on $B$; in
particular no descent of an object or of a morphism of a derived
category is needed below.
1. *constancy along the affine line.* There is a canonical
isomorphism
$$
\kappa:\;F\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;a^*C(g,s).
$$
Since $i_1^*a^*C(g,s)=C(g,s)=i_1^*F$ by

1. *normalization and uniqueness.* $\kappa$ is the unique

restricts to the identity of $C(g,s)$ under the identification
$i_1^*F\simeq C(g,s)$ of
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1).
1. *locality and base change.* $\kappa$ is compatible with
etale localization on $B$ and with arbitrary base change
$B'\to B$.

proof.text:
The family object is the one of [def-pur-dnc-section-family]; tensor inverses and shifts are understood as in [def-weil-derived-tensor].
Write $a:\mathbf A^1_B\to B$ and let $i_1:B\to\mathbf A^1_B$ be the
unit section.

Step 1: the family object is a shift of a lisse rank-one line. By
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](2),
$\widetilde g$ is smooth, so $\omega_{\widetilde g}$ is invertible
by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]; by (2) and (4) it is etale-locally
$\Lambda(d)[2d]$, hence so is $F$. An etale cover of $B$ on
which the pair $(V,s)$ has standard coordinates also carries the
family to the standard model, so
[lem-pur-concentrated-complex-shift] applied to that cover gives

$$
F\;\simeq\;\mathcal L_F(d)[2d],
$$

with $\mathcal L_F$ a finite locally constant rank-one sheaf on
$\mathbf A^1_B$; the same argument gives
$C(g,s)\simeq\mathcal L_1(d)[2d]$ on $B$. This is (1), and this
reduction to actual sheaves is the point which makes the glueing at the
end of the proof the ordinary sheaf axiom.
Step 2: the local models and their normalization. Refine the etale
cover so that in addition $C(g,s)|_{B_i}$ is a shift-twist of the free
rank-one module; such a refinement exists because $C(g,s)$ is finite
locally constant by Step 1. Let $B_i\to B$ be the resulting cover,
on which there are coordinates of pairs
$(V_i,s_i)\to(\mathbf A^d_{B_i},0)$
([lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](2)); for the standard pair the
deformation space is
$\mathbf A^d_{B_i}\times_{B_i}\mathbf A^1_{B_i}$, $x_k=tu_k$.
Exceptional pullback along the coordinate map is ordinary pullback, and
the vector-bundle Thom calculation
([cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] as in
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](4)) supplies an isomorphism

$$
\kappa_i:F|_{\mathbf A^1_{B_i}}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
a_i^*C(g,s)|_{B_i},
$$

whose restriction $\kappa_i(1)$ is an automorphism of the free
rank-one sheaf on $B_i$. Multiplying $\kappa_i$ by the pullback
of its inverse $a_i^*(\kappa_i(1)^{-1})$ normalizes it to the
identity at $t=1$, on every connected component of $B_i$.
Step 3: gluing and uniqueness, i.e. (2) and (3). Apply
[prop-pur-a1-invariance] over the base $Y=B$ with $C=C(g,s)$, with
$\theta:i_1^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}C(g,s)$ the identification of
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1), and with the cover $\{B_i\to B\}$ of
Step 2, whose members may be taken affine, hence separated of finite type
over $k$. Its hypotheses hold: the *local shape* because
$F\simeq\mathcal L_F(d)[2d]$ by Step 1, and the *normalized local
comparisons* are the $\kappa_i$ of Step 2, which restrict at $t=1$ to the
identity of $C(g,s)|_{B_i}$ under $\theta$. Its gluing assertion gives a
unique isomorphism

$$
\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }a^*C(g,s)
$$

restricting to every $\kappa_i$, hence to the identity at $t=1$: this is
(2), and existence in (3). Its uniqueness assertion says that $\kappa$ is
the only isomorphism $F\to a^*C(g,s)$ restricting to $\theta$, i.e. to the
identity of $C(g,s)$, at $t=1$, which is the uniqueness in (3).
Finally, the Rees-algebra description of the DNC
for the closed section, the local standard models, and the localized
Thom classes all commute with base change and etale localization, hence
so does the resulting isomorphism: this is (4).
